minutes.headline: Cable committee voted to hire a studio design expert to advise on the new TCP studio, capped at a set maximum.
minutes.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee approved prior minutes, heard the manager's report on music licensing, live basketball broadcasts, equipment purchases and finances, and discussed the TCP architects. The committee voted by roll call to hire a studio expert to assist the TCP architects, with a not-to-exceed cap. The next meeting was set for January 4 and the meeting adjourned.

what_happened.line: The Public Access Cable Committee voted by roll call to hire a studio design expert to assist the TCP architects, with a not-to-exceed cap.
The manager was directed to find secure storage at the high school, start with one camera and look into an announcer for live basketball.
Members informally agreed the manager may buy a studio countdown clock up to a set limit without a motion.
The manager is to send another urgent request through the Mass Access network for studio design consultants.
The committee approved prior minutes and set its next meeting for January 4.

why_it_matters: The new TCP studio is being designed now, and the consultant's fee and advice will shape how cable access money is spent on the space.
Live local basketball broadcasts and equipment purchases, paid partly through the state under the CARES Act, set what the public access station can offer residents.
watch_next: Whether the Mass Access network request produces studio design consultants and a contract within the cap.
